page.layout: One page of text, no margin notes. Running text in full lines, with numbered paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 and a catchword and signature at the foot.

main_text.p: infeliciter confluxerunt. Id ne papatui affingi à me conqueraris, ecce tibi luculenta hujus rei testimonia.

1. Samaritani provocarunt ad traditiones quas à patribus suis acceperant, Epiph hæref.9. Papistæ accusant scripturas imperfectionis, & necessitatem traditionum non-scriptarum urgent. Vide enchirid. Cosleri[?] p. 47.

2. Nazareni dixerunt libros legis esse fi-ctos, Epiph. hærel. 18. Papistæ quærunt, unde sciamus libros Moisis esse Moisis? unde sciamus libros euangeliftarum esse divinitus in-spiratos? qui sciamus eos non esse adulterinos & suppositiitios? Pighius[?] hierarch. eccles. lib. 1. c. 2. fol. 4.
3. Basilidiani & Carpocratita celarunt doctrinam suam, ac dixerunt: Nos sumus homines, cæteri omnes sunt canes & porci. Ne ꝓji-cite[?] ergo margaritas porcis, & sanctum canib.

Et qui eos redarguebant ex scripturis, eos accusabant, tanquam non redarguentes, & auctoritate nulla valentes. Adde quod veritate non intelligere docerent, nisi eos, qui traditiones novisset, & veritatem non tradi p-scripturam, sed per vivam vocem. Vide Irenæum l.1.c. 2. & 3. Epiph. hær. 24. Papistæ haud sec loquuntur, quando laicos legere scripturas prohibent. Vide Albertum Pium in epist. ad Eras-mum. Ledesimam Jesuitam in lib. de scriptura.

page.notes: Printed page number "143" at top, with a dot. Doubtful readings marked [?]: "Cosleri" (possibly Costeri or Cofferi), "Pighius" (the printed word looks like Tfighim), the abbreviation for "pro" in "Ne ꝓji-cite" (the glyph is unclear), and the catchword "lectiones". "Ne pji-" is a broken word; the reading "projicite" is an inference, so the [?] stays. The break before "Et qui eos" is a judgement from the line length. "Epiph hæref.9." and "18" are uncertain in their exact form. No running head is printed.
